_comment: [Claude 2026-09-02 12:00 MSK] The settings a production job should carry, and why. Every one
of these is a measurement in this notebook rather than a default someone liked.

EVAL_EVERY_FRAMES.why: one evaluation costs about 123 s on a T4 and about 164 s under four-way packing. At 25,000 a 500k run spends about 10% of itself evaluating and returns a 21-point curve; at 10,000 it spends 20%.

EVAL_EPISODES.why: patch P14 turns num_eval_episodes into episodes-per-scene over ten certified scenes, so 2 means one episode per scene. This is the CURVE, deliberately cheap and deliberately noisy; the scientific grid is computed offline from the checkpoint.

SAVE_EVERY_FRAMES.why: the cadence at which upstream's loop already saves. Combined with RLVIGEN_PRESERVE_SNAPSHOTS it turns a 500k run into ten evaluable policies instead of one, at no training cost.

RLVIGEN_PRESERVE_SNAPSHOTS.value: 1 for the RL-ViGen five, considered per baseline elsewhere
RLVIGEN_PRESERVE_SNAPSHOTS.why: ten DrQ-v2 snapshots are 1.0 GiB and ten DrQ ones 5.4 GiB against 20.2 GiB free in the container, multiplied by the number of packed cells. Set it where the budget curve is wanted and the disk allows.

CELL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS.why: soda was cut off at exactly its 3,000 s cap with 8,500 of 10,000 frames done. The cap protected the other two cells in that job; it also cost that cell, and the fix is a cap sized from the measured rate.

offline_grid_episodes_per_scene.why: measured: at one episode per scene the held-out gap is 1.24x the same-scene gap, which is noise; at twenty it is 3.58x with non-overlapping intervals. Coefficient of variation is 0.96 to 2.35, so the pooled ten-scene regime mean has 12.5% standard error at 20 and 25% at 5.
